candidate_sources.title: Boxwood Blight (BP-203-W) — Purdue Plant and Pest Diagnostic Laboratory
candidate_sources.snippet: PLANT AND PEST DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY BP-203-W ppdl.purdue.edu Boxwood Blight. Dedicated extension factsheet covering symptoms (brown leaf spots, black stem streaks/lesions, rapid defoliation), the pathogen Calonectria pseudonaviculata, and management.

candidate_sources.title: Boxwood Blight | Home and Garden Education Center | University of Connecticut
candidate_sources.snippet: Initial symptoms include light or dark brown leaf spots often with dark borders; the fungus forms black, diamond-shaped lesions on stem tissue and causes extensive defoliation. White spore masses on the underside of infected leaves signify C. buxicola. Management relies on prevention, sanitation, and fungicides (chlorothalonil, tebuconazole).

candidate_sources.title: Boxwood Blight | University of Delaware Cooperative Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Dedicated factsheet on boxwood blight caused by Calonectria pseudonaviculata (syn. Cylindrocladium pseudonaviculatum / C. buxicola). Describes dark leaf spots coalescing into brown blotches, black stem streaks, leaf drop, susceptible Buxus species, and alternate hosts Pachysandra and Sarcococca.

candidate_sources.title: Boxwood Blight – Wisconsin Horticulture (UW-Madison Division of Extension)
candidate_sources.snippet: Extension article on boxwood blight: brown leaf spots with concentric rings, black diamond-shaped stem lesions, defoliation; favored by temperatures of 64–80°F and high humidity. Covers cultural controls and fungicide options.

candidate_sources.snippet: APS Plant Disease research article examining soil inoculum production, survival, and infectivity of the boxwood blight pathogen Calonectria pseudonaviculata.

candidate_sources.title: Volutella Blight Disease of Boxwood | University of Maryland Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Volutella stem and leaf blight is caused by the fungal pathogen Pseudonectria buxi (formerly Volutella buxi). Leaves on the tips of infected branches turn red, then bronze and finally yellow, and infected branches die back. The fungus produces salmon pink fruiting bodies on leaves and stems in moist weather. Pseudonectria buxi is an opportunistic pathogen mostly associated with stressed plants. Management includes pruning out diseased branches, improving air circulation, sanitizing tools, and fungicides (chlorothalonil, thiophanate methyl, propiconazole, copper, mancozeb).

candidate_sources.title: Volutella Blight, or Pseudonectria Canker / Home and Landscape / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Volutella blight, or Pseudonectria canker, is caused by Pseudonectria buxi (anamorph Volutella buxi). Dark, sunken lesions and cankers form on stem material and may lead to die-back and leaf drop. The disease is identified by the growth of pink or rusty fuzz on the underside of the leaf, followed by rapid discoloration of leaves. Pruning wounds are a common source of establishment and the pathogen is spread through contaminated pruning tools.

candidate_sources.title: A Diagnostic Guide for Volutella Blight Affecting Buxaceae | Plant Health Progress
candidate_sources.snippet: A Diagnostic Guide for Volutella Blight Affecting Buxaceae. Volutella blight, caused by Pseudonectria buxi (and Pseudonectria foliicola), affects boxwood (Buxus spp.) and other Buxaceae. The guide details symptoms, signs (salmon-colored sporodochia), pathogen morphology, and diagnostic distinctions from boxwood blight (Calonectria pseudonaviculata).

candidate_sources.title: Landscape disease report: Volutella stem and leaf blight on boxwood (Buxus spp.) // University of Missouri IPM
candidate_sources.snippet: Volutella stem and leaf blight, caused by Pseudonectria buxi, is a common boxwood disease in landscapes and nurseries. Pseudonectria buxi overwinters in boxwood branches, leaves and plant debris and causes infection under favorable weather conditions (68°F to 77°F and relative humidity > 85%). Pruning wounds are a common source of establishment and the pathogen can be readily spread through contaminated pruning tools.
